# swarmops commit

Record a changeset from a list of changes; with --advance, also move that ref to it.

```yaml
title: "swarmops commit"
description: "Record a changeset from a list of changes; with --advance, also move that ref to it."
group: "write"
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
mcp_tool: "commit"
envelope_op: "commit"
exit_codes: [0, 1, 2, 4, 5]
errors: [E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED, E_TOO_LARGE, E_EMPTY_COMMIT, E_TYPE_CONFLICT, E_CAS_MISMATCH, E_INVALID_ARG]
syntax: "swarmops commit [OPTIONS] --message <MESSAGE> --changes <FILE>"
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops commit [OPTIONS] --message <MESSAGE> --changes <FILE>
```

## Required arguments

### `--message`

Syntax: `-m, --message <MESSAGE>`.

The commit message.

### `--changes`

Syntax: `--changes <FILE>`.

A JSON file holding an array of changes, or - for stdin: at most 64 MiB.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--parent`

Syntax: `--parent <REV>`.

The changeset to commit on top of (default: main's head, if main exists).

### `--allow-empty`

Syntax: `--allow-empty`.

Record the changeset even if it changes nothing.

### `--advance`

Syntax: `--advance <REF>`.

Also move REF (main or release/&lt;name&gt;) to the new changeset, in the same transaction: both are recorded, or neither.

The move happens only if REF still names --parent (for a root commit, only if REF does not exist yet), so it is always a one-step fast-forward. Give --parent as the full changeset id you read REF at (from ref list, show, log or a commit's result): a ref name resolves when the command runs, and without --parent the commit builds on REF's head as it is then, so the move catches only a race from that moment on.

After E\_CAS\_MISMATCH nothing was recorded, neither the changeset nor the move: commit your change without --advance and land it (swarmops land merges it onto REF's head), or re-apply your edits to the content at the error's `actual` and commit with --parent &lt;actual&gt; --advance REF. Do not re-send your old whole-file puts: they would revert the winner's edits to shared files.

### `--key`

Syntax: `--key <UUID>`.

A uuid v7 (RFC 9562) that makes a retry of this commit safe: make a new one for each commit, and give it again only to retry that commit.

The commit signs at the key's time, to the second, and records the key as its commit\_key metadata, so the same command run again on the same parent makes the same changeset, which the store holds already: the result says replayed: true, with the first run's changeset, and nothing is written. A commit whose parent is the changeset its key made (without --parent, main's head, or REF's with --advance) replays that changeset instead of committing it again on top of itself.

Give --parent as the full changeset id you read: without it the commit builds on main's head (REF's, with --advance) as it is when the command runs, so a retry after that head moved to another changeset commits again, on the new head.

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
SWARMOPS_RUN_ID=run-1 swarmops --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17 commit -m 'first commit

with a body' --changes [tmp]/changes.json
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "op": "commit",
  "api": 1,
  "result": {
    "changeset": "[c1]",
    "root": "[root1]",
    "files_changed": 6,
    "blobs_written": 6,
    "replayed": false
  },
  "meta": {
    "repo": "[tmp]/store",
    "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
    "resolved": {},
    "auth": "trust"
  }
}
```

Exit code 0. Recorded by the CLI tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time.

### MCP

## Return information

`result` is a `CommitResp` (`swarmops schema CommitResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `advanced` | `Advanced or null` | no | The move of the ref the request's `advance` named: present exactly when the ref names `changeset` because of this request, or of an identical one before it (`already_applied`). A request with `advance` whose response lacks it went to a store that ignores the field, and moved no ref. |
| `blobs_written` | `integer` | yes | How many blobs this commit's own writes placed in the object store; blobs that were there already, or that a concurrent writer placed first, count 0. |
| `changeset` | `string` | yes | The new changeset's id. |
| `files_changed` | `integer` | yes | How many paths the changeset changes. |
| `parent` | `string or null` | no | The changeset it was committed on top of; omitted for a root commit. |
| `replayed` | `boolean` | no | The store held the changeset already, from an identical request before (a retry with the same `idempotency_key`), so nothing was written. Always written; a response from a store that does not know the field reads as `false`. |
| `root` | `string` | yes | The new root tree's id. |
| `warnings` | `array of string` | no | Problems found after the commit became durable, such as failed housekeeping; the commit itself succeeded. Omitted when empty. |

Envelope `op`: `commit`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `1`: The operation failed.
- `2`: The request or the command line is malformed.
- `4`: The operation can succeed when it is run again.
- `5`: An identity or policy requirement refused the operation.

## Errors

- [`E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#e_identity_required) (exit 5): A mutation was asked for without an identity.
- [`E_TOO_LARGE`](../errors.md#e_too_large) (exit 1): The content is larger than the operation allows.
- [`E_EMPTY_COMMIT`](../errors.md#e_empty_commit) (exit 1): The commit changes nothing and `allow_empty` is off.
- [`E_TYPE_CONFLICT`](../errors.md#e_type_conflict) (exit 1): A change puts an entry below a file, or a file onto a directory.
- [`E_CAS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#e_cas_mismatch) (exit 4): The ref no longer holds the expected target (or, with `create`, exists at another one); `details.actual` holds what it does, `null` when the ref does not exist.
- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2): A malformed argument or request, including a command-line usage error.

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
